title: Pauri 2, sound: hukmee hovan
hookLine: hukmee hovan aakaar, hukam na kahiaa jaaee
tomorrow: Pauri 2, meaning: all within the order

lines: A CHORUS THAT STARTS THE SAME.
cards: Some songs hook you with their first word, because they keep coming back to it. By the second verse you're singing along before you know the rest. Kids' songs do it.

Protest chants do it. The second pauri of Japji does it too. Yesterday's last word, hukam, becomes today's first, and then it comes back in every line that follows, like a drum you can't stop hearing.

teach.b: The opening line: hukmee hovan aakaar, hukam na kahiaa jaaee. Sound it. Hukmee: HUK-mee, hukam with an ending that means by, or through: by the order.
Hovan: HO-van, they come to be. Aakaar: aa-KAAR, forms, shapes. Then the second half.
Hukam: the plain word again. Na kahiaa jaaee: na, not; KAH-i-aa, said; JAA-ee, can be. You can already feel it: by the order, forms come to be; the order itself can't be said.
The full meaning comes tomorrow. Today, the build. The same word comes back in both halves of the next lines.

Hukmee hovan jeea, hukam milai vadiaaee: by the order, living beings; by the order, greatness. Hukmee utam neech, hukam likh dukh sukh paaeeah: by the order, high and low; by the written order, sorrow and joy.
A drumbeat: hukmee, hukam, hukmee, hukam.

teach.h: THE SAME WORD IN EVERY LINE.
teach.b: Then the pauri gathers everything up in one line with a lovely turn in its sound: hukmai andar sabh ko, baahar hukam na koe. Everyone is inside the order; outside the order, no one.

teach.h: ANDAR AND BAAHAR — IN AND OUT.
teach.b: Hear how andar, inside, and baahar, outside, answer each other. And the last line brings in a word you met in camp three, with seva and ego: haumai.
What the pauri says about it waits for tomorrow.

how: The second pauri of Japji, with its repeated hukmee, is recited each morning; many Sikhs know its rhythm by heart before they study its meaning.

o: a song sung only at weddings
the divine order that all forms come by
a rule only priests are able to explain

games.q: match the sound to its sense.

s: the same word comes back in every line of the second pauri
hukmee and hukam, by the order: a drumbeat.
the pauri says some things are outside the order
everyone is inside the order; outside it, no one.
hukmee and hukam are unrelated words
hukmee is hukam with an ending meaning by, or through.

games.q: the first line says forms come to be by the order. what does it say about the order itself?
o: it can be written down in full.
games.why: hukam na kahiaa jaaee: the order can't be put into words.

practice: Say the first line slowly, out loud if you can: hukmee hovan aakaar, hukam na kahiaa jaaee, three times, slower, then softer.

Then, on each out-breath, just the drumbeat, hukmee, until it goes quiet and you're sitting with what your body does on its own: the heart, the breath, the small sounds. If you pray, you can rest in Waheguru.

wordCard.voice: Hukam. The divine order, the command that every line of this pauri turns on, by it: hukmee, by the order.

orig.s: ਹੁਕਮੀ ਹੋਵਨਿ ਆਕਾਰ ਹੁਕਮੁ ਨ ਕਹਿਆ ਜਾਈ
orig.say: HUK-mee HO-van aa-KAAR, HUK-am na KAH-i-aa JAA-ee
orig.note: Gurmukhi: the opening line of Japji's second pauri.

carryVoice: Your line: hukmee. By the order, and nothing outside of it. Day one hundred sixty-five.
